newsitem.title: UK: Next stage of UK gas competition to start Nov 1. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Next stage of UK gas competition to start Nov 1. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: The next phase of domestic market opening in the U.K. gas industry regulator will start on November 1, gas industry regulator Ofgas said on Monday.

On November 1, 2.5 million customers in Scotland and Durham, Hartlepool, Middlesbrough, Northumberland, Redcar and Cleveland, Stockton-on-Tees and Tyne and Wear will be able to buy gas from any licensed supplier.
The market will open fully in six stages. The second stage, covering 2.8 million customers in Cumbria, Greater Manchester, Hull, Lancashire, and Yorkshire will start on February 27, 1998.
(Deletes incorrect reference to Lincolnshire in above paragraph).

A month later on March 27, a further 2.9 million customers in northern England will follow. On April 24 (corrects from April 4), 3.2 milion customers in Wales and western England have their markets opened.
Most of the Home Counties around London, with 2.1 million customers, open on May 22. London itself and Surrey will be the last area to open up.
A total of 3.1 million customers there will be able to buy their gas from any licensed supplier on June 19, 1998.

This will complete a process started in April 1996, when the southwestern counties of Devon, Cornwall and Somerset became the first area to take part in a pilot trial and get the chance to buy gas from any supplier.

A second area, covering Avon, Dorset, Kent, and East and West Sussex was opened in two phases in February. By June 20, a total of 377,000 customers out of two million in these areas had switched suppliers away from former monopoly holder British Gas Plc.

The supply business of British Gas has been taken over by Centrica Plc since the demerger of the former monopoly holder into Centrica and BG Plc. Bills have fallen by more than 20 percent in some cases for customers switching suppliers.
